result.summary: This residential street features continuous sidewalks on both sides and a marked bike lane, providing basic infrastructure for non-motorized transport. However, the wide roadway and lack of marked pedestrian crossings or traffic calming measures may encourage higher vehicle speeds and create safety risks for people crossing the street.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking on both sides of the street can obscure pedestrians, especially children, from the view of oncoming drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both curbs throughout the visible block.

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossings
hazards.description: There are no visible marked crosswalks or pedestrian warning signs along this stretch of residential road.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at potential crossing points to increase pedestrian visibility and reduce the crossing distance.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Add marked crosswalks with high-visibility paint to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming Measures
interventions.description: Implement speed humps or cushions to reduce vehicle speeds in this residential area.

result.summary: The environment is a residential row-house street dominated by a wide, multi-lane roadway with no visible pedestrian crossing infrastructure. While sidewalks are present, they are interrupted by a large alleyway opening, and parked vehicles significantly obstruct sightlines between pedestrians and motorists.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles, particularly the black truck, are positioned right at the edge of the alleyway entrance, blocking the view of pedestrians for oncoming traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Right foreground at the alleyway entrance

hazards.name: Lack of Protected Crossing
hazards.description: A wide, multi-lane road with no marked crosswalks or pedestrian signals forces pedestrians to cross unprotected.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the main roadway in the foreground

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the alleyway entrance to improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the alleyway to shorten the pedestrian crossing distance and prevent illegal parking that blocks sightlines.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Install a marked, high-visibility crosswalk with appropriate signage to designate a safe crossing point.

result.summary: The image shows a wide residential street with sidewalks on both sides and a designated bus lane. The environment lacks significant pedestrian safety features like buffers or traffic calming, and the wide roadway may encourage higher vehicle speeds.

hazards.name: Wide Roadway
hazards.description: The wide, multi-lane roadway design can encourage higher vehicle speeds in a residential area.

hazards.name: Frequent Driveway Curb Cuts
hazards.description: Multiple driveways along the sidewalk create frequent conflict points between pedestrians and vehicles.

hazards.name: Lack of Sidewalk Buffer
hazards.description: The sidewalk is directly adjacent to the curb with no physical buffer from moving traffic.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at intersections to reduce crossing distance and improve pedestrian visibility.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Buffers
interventions.description: Add a planting strip or street trees between the sidewalk and the curb to provide a physical and psychological buffer.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming Measures
interventions.description: Implement speed humps or raised crosswalks to slow down vehicle traffic.

result.summary: The image depicts a residential street with row houses and a continuous sidewalk separated from the roadway by a narrow grass buffer and parallel parking. While the pedestrian walkway is clear and in good condition, the presence of parked vehicles creates visual obstructions for anyone attempting to cross the street mid-block.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb block the sightlines between drivers and pedestrians, particularly children, who might attempt to cross the street mid-block.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions

interventions.title: Street Trees
interventions.description: Plant street trees in the buffer zone to provide shade and create a vertical element that naturally encourages slower driving speeds.
